Indian Tourist Killed in Helicopter Collision Near Everest Base Camp

03 Nov 2026, 05:51 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

2 min read

Key takeawaysAn Indian tourist has died and others were injured following a mid-air collision between two helicopters near the base camp of Mount Everest in Nepal, according to local officials reporting to the BBC. The incident occurred at approximately 08:15 local time (02:30 GMT) in Pheriche, located roughly 12 kilometers south of the Mount Everest Base Camp.

Incident Overview

An Indian tourist has died and others were injured following a mid-air collision between two helicopters near the base camp of Mount Everest in Nepal, according to local officials reporting to the BBC. The incident occurred at approximately 08:15 local time (02:30 GMT) in Pheriche, located roughly 12 kilometers south of the Mount Everest Base Camp.

According to verified footage and official statements:

  • The blades of the two aircraft clipped as they reportedly attempted to land at the same spot.
  • Fishtail Air identified the deceased tourist as Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu.
  • A New Zealand tourist and the Fishtail Air pilot sustained injuries and were subsequently rescued and transported to Kathmandu.
  • The second helicopter, operated by Air Dynasty, was carrying cargo with a single crew member on board who reportedly sustained no injuries.

Practical Transport and Seasonal Context

Nepal's rugged topography makes helicopters an essential mode of transport for remote mountain regions. However, aviation operations in the Himalayas are frequently challenged by high altitudes and rapidly fluctuating weather patterns.

  • Destination: Nepal (Solukhumbu district).
  • Seasonal Considerations: Autumn is a peak period for trekking and climbing expeditions in the region, including routes near Mount Everest and Ama Dablam.
  • Village of Pheriche: Situated at an altitude of just over 4,000 meters (13,120 feet) above sea level along a major trekking path.

Official Guidance and Verification

Travelers planning visits to high-altitude Himalayan regions should review updated safety advisories and transportation protocols before departure.

  • Official Resources: Consult announcements from the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal and official tourism portals for updated transport regulations.
  • Advisory Notice: Mountain aviation inherently carries risks. Official travel advisories do not guarantee absolute safety or entry conditions, and itineraries should remain flexible to account for weather and logistical changes.
